clue.text: Capital way for Polly to exercise?

definitions.text: Capital way for Polly to exercise?

parts.words: Capital way for Polly to exercise?
parts.note: read as a London street whose name suggests a place where a pet parrot (Polly) might stretch its legs

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about where a pet parrot might take a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly is the stock name for a parrot. Birdcage Walk is a real street in London, running beside St James's Park, so 'Capital way' is a road in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a road in Westminster, London, named for the royal aviary once kept there, and the name pictures a cage for a parrot.

clue.text: Something from hatter I brought back?

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about some item a hat-maker brought back with them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the vague 'Something', but the surface hints it is a hat: the hidden run sits in 'hatter I brought', read from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's square cap is a thing, so the bare word stands for any object; the hatter in the surface hints at headwear.

clue.text: Abusing safety feature on flight, perhaps

definitions.meaning: berating someone bitterly, as in complaining loudly against them
a flight of stairs has a barrier along its edge to stop people falling

explanation.surface: Someone misusing a safety device on an aeroplane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an aeroplane, but here it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail at someone is to scold them harshly; a banister-like barrier guards the side of a staircase.

clue.text: Shortened — so brief, girl's upset

parts.note: curt means brief or terse in speech

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the name is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Delia is a girl's name; the 's stands for 'has' or possession and gives no letter

explanation.surface: A girl is upset because something was cut short and abrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' in a down clue turns the girl's name upside down; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut back or reduced in length has been abridged.

clue.text: Easy tasks, like turning over stone-fruit

indicators.note: turning over means the joined pieces are read in reverse order, from the bottom up

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
a fig is a fruit

explanation.surface: Easy jobs compared to flipping a stone-fruit such as a plum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone-fruit' looks like one thing (a plum or peach) but splits in two. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds; 'turning over' reads the pair from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a gift is so easy it might as well be given away, so easy tasks are presents in slang.

clue.text: Justify belligerent tirade

parts.note: war, used as an adjective (a war footing), means belligerent or warlike
a rant is a long angry tirade

explanation.surface: Defending an aggressive verbal outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: To give grounds or sanction for something is to vindicate it.

clue.text: Oriental national doesn't begin to change

indicators.note: to change says the remaining letters are rearranged
doesn't begin means the word national loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A national of an Eastern country who never starts to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental national' looks like the definition together; only 'Oriental' defines, and 'national' is the fodder. 'doesn't begin' drops its N, leaving ATIONAL, which 'to change' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Laos in Southeast Asia is Eastern, the old sense of oriental.

clue.text: Rump? Not enough to cat

definitions.meaning: the Rump Parliament was the House of Commons cut down after Pride's Purge, so a reduced lower house
meagre rations, an old phrase for scanty food allowances

explanation.surface: A rump steak that does not make a full meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rump' suggests a cut of beef; it is the Rump Parliament of 1648, a House of Commons left short of members.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means scanty rations, from commons, the food shared at a college table; a curtailed House of Commons is the punning second sense.

clue.text: Worrying type gets the bird

definitions.meaning: one who harries, that is pesters or worries others
a hawk of open country, as in the hen variety

explanation.surface: An anxious person ends up being jeered at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' looks like the idiom for being booed; it simply joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pesterer who keeps harassing is one sense; the other is a bird of prey that hunts low over moorland.

clue.text: Distance boa extended

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf of fur or feathers
long means extended in length

explanation.surface: A snake stretched out over some distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boa' looks like the snake; here it is the fur stole.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a measure of length, an eighth of a mile, still used in horse racing.

clue.text: Novel fellow married girl with the usual token

parts.note: guy means a fellow or man
Anne is a girl's name
a ring is the customary token of a wedding

explanation.surface: A man married a girl and gave her the customary wedding band.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is by Sir Walter Scott (1815).
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a Waverley book by Scott, so it is a work of long fiction.

clue.text: Wine canister, unopened, is returned

indicators.note: returned says the remaining letters are read backwards
unopened means the word canister loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tin of wine that has not been opened is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' takes the C from canister, leaving ANISTER, and 'returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: If in frightening circumstances, scratch

indicators.note: in says the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: scary describes frightening circumstances
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being scratched in a scary situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To make shallow cuts or scrape the skin or soil is the sense here.

clue.text: Archbishop pronounced see initially sound as a bell

indicators.note: initially puts the sound of see at the start, before the archbishop
pronounced says the word see is to be taken by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: see is said like the letter C
Cosmo Gordon Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942

explanation.surface: An archbishop declared his diocese to sound as clear as a bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a bishop's diocese, which fits 'Archbishop'; here it is just its sound, the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic noise is what a struck bell makes.

clue.text: Ill-fated liner for us in 25, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters may come in another order, so they are to be rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, a word for a person from Rome or Milan

explanation.surface: A doomed ocean liner meant for Americans in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: US in the letters of 25's answer, 'perhaps' rearranged, gives the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cunard ship was torpedoed in 1915 with great loss of life, so it was a doomed passenger vessel.

clue.text: Entrance is a nuisance after a time

indicators.note: after says the nuisance word comes after the period of time

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a bind is a nuisance or chore in British slang

explanation.surface: A doorway that becomes a nuisance after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun (a door); it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable. 'after' puts the nuisance behind the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone rapt as if by magic is to enchant them.

clue.text: Deal badly with South getting cards in the long run

indicators.note: in says the south and cards pieces go inside the running distance

parts.note: a mile is a classic long running race
a hand is the set of cards a player holds

explanation.surface: A bridge player in the South seat plays the cards badly over a long session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' and 'cards' suggest a card game; 'in the long run' looks like the idiom for eventually but gives MILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle something clumsily or incompetently is to botch it.

clue.text: Main weapon for fish

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open ocean
a pike is a long spear carried by foot soldiers

explanation.surface: The chief weapon for catching fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective (chief); it is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a name for the hake and other long-jawed ocean species.

clue.text: Christian name of a famous surgeon

parts.note: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: Asking for the first name of a celebrated surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a surgeon's first name; the answer is a first name itself, built from A and the surgeon's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a male given name, a Scottish form of Alexander.

clue.text: Military staff to maintain stand

definitions.meaning: a field marshal carries a short rod as a mark of rank
in cricket, to keep batting and extend a partnership

explanation.surface: Army officers are told to hold their position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like personnel; it is a stick. The second sense is a cricket phrase: a batting stand is a partnership, and to keep it going is to carry on batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal's ceremonial rod is one sense; the other splits as a phrase for continuing to bat in cricket.

clue.text: One of Bill's victims near Niagara Falls

definitions.meaning: William Cody earned his nickname by shooting thousands of American bison
a city in New York state close to the falls

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill harmed a person near Niagara Falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like any man; it is the frontiersman named after the animals he hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bison is the beast Cody hunted; the same word names a city on Lake Erie by the falls.

clue.text: Four or six in test? It's not important

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test
VI is the Roman numeral for six; IV for four, put after TR, gives the same word

explanation.surface: A cricket question: is a boundary in a Test match of no account?
explanation.walkthrough: Either numeral works: TR + IV + IAL or TRI + VI + AL. 'Four or six' and 'test' suggest cricket boundaries in a Test match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of little significance or worth is petty.

clue.text: Nothing bad in abbreviated version of this book

definitions.text: Nothing bad in abbreviated version of this book

parts.words: Nothing bad in abbreviated version of this book
parts.note: the short form of an Old Testament book's name reads as O for nothing followed by BAD

explanation.surface: This book's abridged edition contains nothing harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual abbreviation of the book's name is Obad., which splits as O (nothing) and BAD, so its short form literally has 'nothing bad' in it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the shortest book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Man names a tropical shrub

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
n is the abbreviation for name, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A man gives a name to a plant from the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'names' looks like a verb; it gives N twice, the abbreviation for name made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Old World plant whose leaves yield a reddish dye for hair and skin.

clue.text: Higher position of connexion between sides

indicators.note: between says the pieces sit inside the two side letters

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the two sides
taken as written
a tie is a connection or bond

explanation.surface: A higher placing for a link joining two sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' are left and right, and 'between' puts the middle pieces inside them; 'position' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: More elevated or more lofty in height or manner, the comparative of tall-standing.

clue.text: Struck with glove, you'll require second, for a start

indicators.note: for a start says the abbreviation goes at the front of the glove word

parts.note: a mitten is a glove without separate fingers

explanation.surface: Slapped with a glove in a duel challenge, you will need a second.
explanation.walkthrough: In duelling, a challenge was a slap with a glove and each fighter needed a second; here 'second' gives just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit, as a past participle of to smite; also used for being lovestruck.

clue.text: National symphony composed by German

definitions.meaning: a citizen of a southern European country
Mendelssohn, a German composer, wrote his Symphony No. 4 after travelling south of the Alps

explanation.surface: A patriotic symphony written by a German composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective qualifying 'symphony'; it is a noun, a citizen, and the symphony is a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Rome is one sense; Mendelssohn's Fourth Symphony carries the same nickname.

clue.text: Has old nature reformed in thorough fashion

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone whose old character has been reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with complete commitment and energy is doing it wholeheartedly.
